newsitem.title: USA: High-level White House meeting on Middle East set.
newsitem.headline: High-level White House meeting on Middle East set.

text.p: Members of U.S. President Bill Clinton's Middle East advisory team converged on the White House on Thursday to discuss how to advance the peace process after Wednesday's suicide bombings in Jerusalem.

Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, who cut short an Asian trip to attend, Middle East mediator Dennis Ross and National Security Adviser Sandy Berger were to take part in the meeting, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.
The meeting, which was to take place on Thursday afternoon, followed Wednesday's twin suicide bombings at a Jerusalem market that killed 15 people and wounded more than 150.
It was the deadliest attack since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won election in 1996 vowing to bolster security. The Islamic militant movement Hamas claimed responsibility.

McCurry said Clinton's aides will discuss developments and "next steps" in the stalemated peace process, and said Clinton was not expected to attend. "I doubt very much they will present recommendations to the president at this point. It's more of an assessment meeting," he said.

Clinton on Wednesday condemned the latest violent deed in the Middle East as a barbarous act, and called on Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to take concrete steps to strengthen security in the region.

The law that makes it possible for the United States to have official dealings with and give aid to Arafat's Palestinian Authority expires on Aug. 12, and the White House faces significant congressional opposition to extending it.
Expiration of the act would end U.S. aid to Palestinians, stop diplomatic contacts and force the Palestinian Liberation Office to close its Washington office.

Asked if the president was satisfied with Arafat's pledge that he is committed to ensuring a secure environment for Israel, McCurry replied, "the president feels the chairman made an appropriate statement, yes, but ... continues to believe that efforts need to be made to strengthen security cooperation."

Clinton also announced Ross will delay a trip to the Middle East that was to have started on Wednesday to permit a period of mourning. Asked when it would be rescheduled, McCurry said, "I'm not going to speculate."
